question: Explain how the small size of the nucleus, the short-range nature of nuclear force and binding energy together show that nucleons form a strongly bound system.

options.A: Nucleons form a strongly bound system only because the nucleus has large size, so their separation is large.
options.B: The short-range nuclear force is too weak at nuclear distances to bind nucleons, and binding energy is unrelated to mass defect.
options.C: Nucleons are confined within a tiny region of order $10^{-15}\,\text{m}$, where short-range attractive nuclear force is strong. The mass defect gives binding energy $E_b=\Delta mc^2$, showing that energy must be supplied to separate the nucleons; together these facts show a strongly bound system.
options.D: Nuclear binding is caused only by electrostatic attraction between protons.
